2026.name: Peace Officers Memorial Day
2026.reason: Honoring federal, state, and local law enforcement officers killed or disabled in the line of duty.

2026.name: Memorial Day
2026.reason: Honoring Americans who died in military service.
2026.note: Half-staff from sunrise until noon only, then raised briskly to the top of the staff for the remainder of the day.

2026.name: National Korean War Veterans Armistice Day
2026.reason: Honoring veterans of the Korean War.
2026.note: The statutory half-staff provision expired after 2003. Half-staff applies only if a proclamation is issued for this specific year. Must be confirmed against live proclamation data — not assumed.

2026.name: Patriot Day
2026.reason: Honoring the individuals who lost their lives in the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001.
2026.note: Statute requests an annual presidential proclamation rather than mandating half-staff directly. Observed every year in practice.

2026.name: National Fallen Firefighters Memorial Service
2026.reason: Honoring firefighters who died in the line of duty, observed during the national memorial service in Emmitsburg, Maryland.
2026.note: DATE IS AN ESTIMATE (historical norm: first Sunday in October). The actual date is set each year by proclamation and must be resolved from live data before display.

2026.name: National Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day
2026.reason: Honoring the individuals who died as a result of their service at Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941.
2026.note: Statute requests an annual presidential proclamation rather than mandating half-staff directly. Observed every year in practice.
